findings.label: Restricted diffusion on DWI
findings.evidence: showing diffusion restriction with no enhancement, indicative of an epidermoid cyst

panels.rationale: The figure is a single axial T2-weighted MRI of the brain showing a hyperintense, space-occupying lesion (indicated by an arrow). The accompanying text explicitly diagnoses this lesion as an intracranial epidermoid cyst, noting its T2 hyperintensity and diffusion restriction.
panels.attribution_text: Aldoseri and Hammad Seroor Jadah. A Rare Case of a Compressive Intracranial Epidermoid Cyst in a 13-Year-Old Patient.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.73197. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: MRI of the brain Axial T2-weighted MRI image showing hyperintense space-occupying lesion (arrow). MRI: magnetic resonance imaging.
in_text_mentions: prepontine cistern, and cerebellopontine angle. The lesion extends to the posterior aspect of the suprasellar cistern in contact with the optic chiasm. The lesion has a significant mass effect on the pons and mesencephalon. It appears hyperintense on T2 and hypointense on T1, showing diffusion restriction with no enhancement, indicative of an epidermoid cyst (Figures 1-3). The neurosurgery team referred the patient for a consultation, advised a watch-and-wait approach, and did not recommend surgical intervention due to the benign nature of the tumor. The harm outweighs the benefit of surgery.
